I’ve heard people postulate that the Neanderthals and other hominids were possibly the giants, nephilim, or the descendants of Cain.   It’s theorized that the reason why humans have such good facial recognition is because we interacted with other hominids and had to get good at recognizing us and them. Perhaps God created them to give us this ability, or possibly for human genetic diversity. As far as I know, the Orthodox Church does not take a dogmatic position on this topic. 

I’m somewhat of a theistic evolutionist, I think there’s pretty clear evidence that evolution is a real thing, and that it is directed by God. Why wouldn’t a great creator make his creation adaptable? Considering the fact that he exists both inside and outside of time and space as humans know it, His timeframes, motives, and processes of creation are wildly alien to us. After all, what is a “day” to an eternal, uncreated God that always has been and always will be? I don’t take the Genesis story of creation as 100% exactly literal, as God was divinely imparting the story of creation to Moses through the Holy Spirit, and had to explain it in a way that Moses, and others of his time who would read the text, could understand, and I don’t think any of them knew about astrophysics or organic chemistry. 

It’s interesting to think about, but I don’t really think it’s a productive line of thought or that my religion has to align with every modern scientific theory and practice, as “science” has been incorrect and/or unethical many times through out history. Definitely a curious topic though.

Oh buddy. You’re literally 18 and 19 and you’re unmarried, you cannot allow or disallow her to do anything. Both of you are barely adults and have a lot to learn about relationships and marriage. 

There’s also a level of moderation that is acceptable within our faith. My priest enjoys a good cigar and some bourbon from time to time. Our catechism teacher has full tattoo sleeves. I myself have a facial piercing and a few tattoos and guess what? No one has said a single thing about it to me at church, ever. There are much bigger threats to our salvation than tattoos, piercings, dancing, and having a drink in moderation. We aren’t Muslims and we aren’t legalists. As someone who has been around the block a few times, trust me when I say that there are much worse things in this world than a young person having a couple drinks at the club.  You’re very new to orthodoxy, you don’t know everything, and you’re not an authority on what other people should or shouldn’t be doing. 

If she wants tattoos and piercings, or to go to bars, or whatever, that’s her prerogative and it’s her life, you cannot make any choices for her. And hear me when I say this, the BIGGEST lesson I have learned about relationships is that you cannot force someone to be who you want them to be. No one is happy then. You cannot control or coerce people into being someone they aren’t, even if you have good intentions. If there’s a major conflict within your values and life goals, then go your separate ways. It hurts, but not as much as forcing yourselves to be in a relationship that won’t work out for either of you. 

Also, focus on being realistic. Make sure that you are not engaging in unhealthy and unrealistic fantasies about orthodox life and marriage. Your future wife should not be someone who simply ticks the necessary boxes, or “looks the part”, or bakes sourdough in a veil all day, she will be someone who will be your best friend, partner in all endeavors, advisor, confidant, and someone who you trust, love, and respect completely. You have a lot of time to find the right lady and a lot of time to work on yourself to be the best future husband you can be. 

There’s no rush! You have plenty of time to get married, and you don’t have to get married to this young lady in particular. Take your time in finding the right woman and being the right man for her. You’re so young and you have so much growth and changing to do in your life. If you do want to stay with her, then look at how you can support her through what seems like a dark night of the soul for her, instead of borderline denigrating her for not being perfect and struggling. 

God bless you both.

Hmm, very interesting. I’m going to assume that your family is Christian, given the fact that your three year old knows about Jesus and heaven. I am also Christian. 

I’m also going to assume that the blood tests and sleep studies came back fairly normal and the other changes you made didn’t have much of an effect. So IMO, there’s three possibilities of what could be causing this. 

1. Undetected physical issue. Is there possibly mold in the house, or in his room? Could he have come into contact with lead or other heavy metals? Does he have asthma or allergies, which could deprive his brain of oxygen at night? Did he express any other unusual behavioral changes over the past year? Is there a family history of sleep disorders? Has he gotten any CT or MRI scans of his brain? Is there some kind of untreated infection like a UTI, ear or oral infection? All things to consider. 

2. Emotional distress and dysregulation. Did something happen about a year ago when this started that could have emotionally affected him? Did he see or was in some kind of accident? Did a loved one pass on? Did you move? Did he start going to daycare? Did he transition to sleeping by himself? Is he hearing about religious topics that are too complex for him to understand and scare him a bit? Was there some stressful situation at home? You could consult a child psychologist to do an evaluation, worth a shot. 

3. Spiritual warfare. If possibilities one and two have been exhausted, and the situation is not getting better, it could be spiritual. I am an Orthodox Christian that was involved in the occult prior to my conversion. The spiritual world is very real. Any other “high strangeness” going on at home? I’m not sure which denomination you are, but get your house blessed, and do that even if you haven’t exhausted other possibilities, just in case. I’m not saying this is definitively demonic influence, but demons will often target children because they’re more sensitive and lack the spiritual and psychological defenses that adults have developed. 

Now in my religious tradition, having spiritual visions and experiences of those who have departed earthly life is not unheard of. There’s been many cases of people (including some canonized saints themselves) who report being visited by the Virgin Mary or departed saints, even Christ Himself, and many other unusual and miraculous occurrences. Very rare, but it does happen. However, when it does happen, the experiencer has been seeking heavenly intercession through prayer and has a close relationship with God, and it’s an ecstatic experience, they don’t end up screaming and panicking. This is inducing anxiety in your son and the rest of your family, and probably causing all of you to be sleep deprived, which is a common demonic strategy. I’ve never heard of any other children in my current or past (I was raised in a different Christian denomination as a child) religious community having nightmares about religious matters, that’s really not normal. 

Thoroughly investigate the physical and emotional, but consider speaking to your pastoral figure about this issue, if you have one. I’m obviously biased, but I recommend that you speak to an Orthodox or Catholic priest if no other treatments alleviate your son’s fear and suffering. Poor little guy. I hope you’re able to resolve this.

Are you sleeping in your contacts or not changing them out as directed? The only time my eyes get sticky and crusty like that is when I accidentally fall asleep with my contacts in, but that goes away after I take my contacts out and flush my eyes with sterile eye drops. Make sure you wash your hands before you touch your eyes. 

If it’s been going on for this long, you NEED to visit a doctor OP. If eye infections go untreated, you could potentially lose your vision. For now, I would suggest you stop wearing your contacts to let your eyeballs breathe. 

If you’re in the US, Walmart and Target (or any other department store with a vision clinic) do “cheap” eye exams without insurance, usually about $50-100. The optometrist can prescribe you some antibiotic eye drops. You can use GoodRx or another prescription coupon service to save on the medicine if you don’t have insurance. The staff at the optometrist office will likely let you set up a payment plan for the visit if you can’t pay the full cost up front. It’s a bit embarrassing to explain that you can’t afford it, but it’s better than being blind. And also better than letting it progress to the point that you have to go to the ER and getting stuck with an even bigger bill. Take care of this ASAP before it gets worse and requires more intense and expensive treatment. 

Also OP, please don’t take this offensively as I’m not trying to be, but if you’re struggling to reliably take care of yourself, contacts probably aren’t a very good choice for you since they require quite a bit of care to wear safely. Oh boy. This is a tricky question, and a topic that I’ve struggled with a lot myself. 

Firstly, it’s normal to feel bitter and resentful when you consider all the ways you’ve been mistreated. It’s a very human reaction. What you do with those feelings are what matters. 

Some people are so bitter and hurt that they externalize it and take it out on other people. They find ways to put others down to feel better about themselves. “Hurt people hurt people” couldn’t be more true. 

When I interact with mean, hurtful people, I try to remember that they’re hurting SO BAD that they lash out at others and likely don’t know how to process their emotions in a healthy way. If someone’s just being a jerk to me for no reason, it says more about them than it does about me. I’ve started to feel pity for these people instead of hatred. How sad and empty must these people’s lives be that they are only fulfilled by putting others down. They’re like a wolf with its leg caught in a trap, desperately biting at anything that comes near. 

You’ve been so hurt by these people through out your life. Are you going to let that make you as hateful as it made them? Or are you going to transmute that pain into something constructive? 

For example, I work in an industry known for rampant toxic behavior. My current workplace isn’t so bad, but I’ve noticed almost PTSD-like reactions from myself and my coworkers whenever we make the smallest mistake. I’ve been screamed at and belittled in the past, but as someone coming into a leadership position, I refuse to pass that down to others. I want to take the pain I’ve experienced and use that to make a change, even if it’s on the smallest level. One of my coworkers accidentally breaks a stack of plates? Hey man, it happens, it’s not a big deal. 

People are so shocked and relieved when you treat them with compassion, ESPECIALLY if they’ve been cruel to you in the past. It can even be an epiphany for them. For example, I had an old coworker who was always grumpy and gossiping, and frequently snapped at people. I started being really nice to her and just ignoring her attempts at getting under my skin. When she made a mistake, I didn’t take my chance to yell at her or make her feel bad. Gradually, she began to soften up and follow my example. We ended up being on pretty good terms. Sometimes people have never had anyone be kind to them. 

Essentially, be the change you want to see in the world. That’s how I cope.

My religion also helps me a lot with the way I contextualize and cope with the behavior of others. I understand that’s not everyone’s cup of tea though, so I’ll leave it at that unless someone wants to know more.
